This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janene Herbst. With just over a week until Election Day, polls suggest Republicans are losing ground as they fight to keep control of Congress.
The final stretch of the campaign is giving both parties little time to persuade undecided voters and get supporters to the polls.
And here's Mara Liasson has more.
Polls show President Trump's overall approval rating at its lowest ever, and his approval rating on the economy in some polls is under 30 percent.
But the polls in the battleground House and Senate races are still very close.
In the dozen or so competitive House races, the generic ballot question, that is, would you rather have a Democrat or Republican represent you in Congress, Democrats are ahead by only two or three points.
And the races that will decide control of the Senate are all too close to call.
In states like Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, and Texas, polls show neither candidate ahead outside the margin of error.
Democrats need to flip net four seats to take the Senate majority.
Donald Trump won all those states in 2024 by double digits.
Mara Liasson, NPR News.
President Trump continues rallying for Republican candidates.
He's in Michigan this afternoon, stumping for Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
That follows a visit to the state yesterday by former President Obama, who delivered a fiery speech to the crowd as he supported U.S. Democratic Senate candidates.
This has control of both chambers of Congress hangs in the balance.
Israel is holding elections this week.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is running for and trailing behind his main opponent, Gadi Isincote, in most polls.
And here's Daniel Estrin has more.
These are the final election polls to be published before Tuesday's vote in Israel.
And most of them have the center-right opposition parties as the frontrunners ahead of Netanyahu's far-right camp.
But most polls also find that neither the opposition nor Netanyahu have a clear path to forming a majority-governing coalition.
Days before elections, Netanyahu has drawn criticism from Israel's central bank for saying in an interview that the country could face international sanctions on its banks
and that Israel would have to rely on cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.
Israel faces growing global isolation and sanctions because of its policies toward Palestinians.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Archdiocese of New York and lawyers for 1,300 people who say they've been sexually abused by clergy have agreed to an $800 million legal settlement.
That's the second biggest involving a Catholic archdiocese in the U.S. following a 2024 settlement of $880 million involving the Archdiocese of Los Angeles.
Abuse survivor attorney Jeff Anderson tells the AP the settlement represents a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice.
You're listening to NPR News.
A new defense technology company plans to use gene editing and cloning to create super dogs for military and police use.
And here's John Ruich reports the company called Warhound just got $200 million in funding.
The company says it plans to rebuild America's domestic supply of elite working dogs for the military, law enforcement and first responders.
It will use colossal biosciences gene editing tools and cloning technology to produce healthier dogs with "characteristics suited to demanding missions."
It will also use defense tech from the company Andoril to give dogs and their handlers better awareness and protection in the field.
In a statement, the Texas-based company says animal welfare is central to the program.
The technology will make the dogs healthier and more durable and limit washouts.
John Ruich, NPR News.
At the weekend box office, DC Studios Clayface took the top spot with an estimated $24 million in ticket sales.
It was produced for a reported $44 million.
That's a fraction of the cost of most comic book films.
That beats A24's documentary "You Can See Everything" on Elizabeth Holmes, which took second place with $19 million in its first weekend.
In third place, "Wildwood," the latest stop motion animated film debuted with $11 million.
"Street Fighter" was in fifth place and "Wicker," a comic fable starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgard debuted with $5 million in fifth place.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
